Radiologically, these findings were highly suggestive of peritoneal mesothelioma (Figure 1).

Top-Right: MRI scan shows heterogeneous lesion and associated peritoneal nodules, consistent with peritoneal mesothelioma presentation. Bottom-Left: Coronal plane MRI demonstrates peritoneal findings of small nodules and a large associated mass between the liver and duodenum, characteristic of mesothelioma. Bottom-Right: Coronal plane MRI shows a large heterogeneous mass and associated nodularity, strongly suggesting peritoneal mesothelioma.

in_text_mentions: from research ethics committee approval. Written informed permission was obtained from the patient to publish the case report and images for scientific purposes. During routine diagnostics, a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan showed a heterogeneous expansive lesion between the right hepatic lobe and duodenum, with partially defined margins, measuring approximately 6.0 x 5.0 cm. The lesion exhibited a hypovascular pattern and was predominantly peripheral to the contrast medium, with several small nodules interpositioned between the surface of the right hepatic lobe and diaphragm (Figure 1).
